We need solve ARC-like. Need infer transformation. Need produce for test unseen. Let's inspect examples.

We have grids with several colored line segments: vertical/horizontal partial lines. Output extends one existing colored line to connect to/align with another marker? Need analyze.

Example1 input 11x11. Nonzero:
color6 at (0,5) singleton? row0 col5.
color4 vertical line at col10 rows1-9 (and row5 output extended). Input rows1-9 col10 =4? row10 none. Actually rows1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 col10=4. length9.
color2 vertical at col0 rows4-6.
color7 at row10 col3.

Output: same, except row5 col1-10 filled with 4. So horizontal line color4 from col1 to col10, at row5, connecting the color2 vertical? Row5 is within vertical 2 (rows4-6 col0). It extends from adjacent to 2 at col0 to existing vertical 4 at col10. Why row5? Maybe intersection/row of middle of color2? Also color6 at (0,5) maybe column of 6? Hmm row5 = column of color6? color6 at col5. Wait output horizontal row5 (index 5) equals column index of 6? Yes 6 at (0,5), so row = col of 6. Extend line of color4 from vertical color2 at col0 to vertical color4 at col10 along row indicated by singleton 6? Check.

Example2 input 14x10. Nonzero:
color7 vertical col7 rows0-4? rows0,1,2,3,4 =7. 
color8 vertical col4 rows3-9? rows3,4,5,6,7,8,9 =8? yes row9 col4=8.
color1 horizontal row12 cols0-3.
Output: add horizontal row6 cols0-4 filled 8. Row6? color1? not. Maybe row6 = ? Existing 8 vertical rows3-9, midpoint? row6 (median) within. Extends left to col0 along row6. Why row6? Maybe row index determined by horizontal color1? Row12? No. Or by gap between vertical 7 and 8? Let's see.

Actually output adds row6 col0-3 =8, plus col4 already 8, so horizontal from left edge to vertical 8. Row6 is central row of vertical 8 segment (rows3-9, length7, middle row6). Extend color8 from its vertical midpoint to left edge? In ex1, vertical 4 rows1-9 length9, midpoint row5. Output horizontal 4 at row5 from col1 to col10, extending from vertical 2? Wait midpoint of color4 vertical segment rows1-9 is row5. Yes! It extends horizontal at midpoint of vertical 4, from col1 to its own column 10. To left until adjacent to vertical 2 at col0? Row5 col0 is 2, so fill col1-10 with 4. So rule: For a vertical line, extend a horizontal line of its color from its middle row toward another object/edge? In ex1 vertical 4 midpoint row5, extends left until before color2 at col0. It doesn't overwrite 2. Why not to edge? Because blocked by vertical 2 at col0 row5. So fills between obstacle and line.

Example2: color8 vertical rows3-9 midpoint row6. Extend horizontal left to edge? Is there object at row6 left? row6 col0-3 zeros, no obstacle; output fills col0-4. It reaches left edge. So rule extend from midpoint of vertical line horizontally in direction of some object? Direction left because maybe color1 horizontal at bottom left indicates? Or because vertical 7 is on right? Hmm.

Example3 input 9x16. Nonzero:
color5 vertical col1 rows0-2 (length3).
color8 at (0,15), and (1,14) maybe diagonal two cells.
color6 singleton at (4,8).
color2 horizontal row7 cols3-11 (length9). Output: row7 changed cols0-11 filled 2, extending left to edge (col0-2 added). This is horizontal line color2, midpoint column? row7 cols3-11 length9, midpoint col7? Wait output extends left from col3 to col0, but not right. Why left? Because color5 vertical at col1 above? Hmm.

Let's identify general: There are lines/segments. Output extends one existing segment along its perpendicular direction at its midpoint to an edge or until another colored cell/line. Which segment selected and direction determined by some cue? Maybe each grid contains a "T" potential: one colored object is a line segment; another small marker aligns with its middle row/column, indicating direction and extension. Need infer.

Ex1: Existing vertical 4 at right. Its midpoint row = row5. There is singleton 6 at (0,5). The row index equals column of singleton 6? Also color2 vertical left intersects row5. Actually singleton 6 at top col5; its column 5 equals midpoint row of 4. Thus the marker 6 indicates which row to draw? But output color is 4, not 6. It connects the vertical 4's midpoint to the left until hitting color2. Hmm marker 6 at col5 lies on row0, not row5.

Maybe transformation: For each object, draw line from its center to nearest edge/object in direction indicated by another object's position? Let's parse all.

Maybe there are "full lines" that get extended to border based on a single cell of same? Wait Example3 output extends horizontal 2 to left edge. Row7 is horizontal 2 segment cols3-11. Its midpoint col7. There is singleton 6 at (4,8), close to col7? Not exact. color5 vertical col1 rows0-2. Its midpoint row1. color8 diagonal at top right. Hmm.

Maybe rule: Lines are extended at their midpoint perpendicular to direction of an external cell located in the same row/column as the midpoint? Check Ex1: vertical 4 midpoint row5. External color2 vertical col0 crosses row5, so intersection to left. Thus extension to left until it hits color2. It is perpendicular from a vertical line at midpoint toward a colored cell in same row (color2 at row5 col0). So yes: For vertical 4, look along its midpoint row. There is color2 at col0, left. Extend color4 from col10 left to just after color2? Actually fills between col1-10, stopping before color2 at col0. So draw horizontal segment from vertical line to the cell/object in that row, excluding obstacle. Why choose color4? It is the vertical line whose midpoint row has another colored object. color2 vertical also crosses row5. Maybe choose longer line? color4 length9 vs color2 length3. It extends longer.

Ex2: vertical 8 midpoint row6. Along row6, no other colored cell? Left edge only. Output extends left to edge. There is horizontal color1 at row12 cols0-3, not same. Maybe row6 midpoint column? Wait vertical 8 at col4 midpoint row6. Looking horizontally at row6, there is no other object; nearest edge left. So extend to edge. What about vertical 7 midpoint row2? Row2 has no other object; could extend? Not done. Why choose 8? Maybe because it is longer? color8 length7, color7 length5. Longer line gets extended. Example1 color4 length9 vs 2 length3, choose longer. Example3 horizontal 2 length9 vs vertical 5 length3, choose longer. Aha selected longest line segment. Extend it perpendicular at its midpoint toward nearest edge? But direction? Ex1 longest vertical 4 midpoint row5; extend left because there is maybe nearest edge? Wait vertical 4 at col10, midpoint row5. The row has obstacle color2 at col0. If simply extend to nearest edge from col10? Nearest edge is right edge col10 already at edge? Actually vertical line at col10 (rightmost). Perpendicular horizontal from col10; two directions left/right. Right edge none. It extends left. Ex2 vertical 8 at col4, midpoint row6. It extends left to edge, not right. Why left? Maybe because longest line's midpoint row has color? Row6: col0-3 zero, col4 8, col5-9 zero. Nearest edge left distance4, right distance5. It extends toward nearer edge! Ex1 at col10, left distance10 vs right0; but right is edge at col10? Can't extend beyond? If considering cells to fill along row excluding line, right side no cells (col>10 none), so only left. Ex3 longest horizontal 2 row7 cols3-11. Midpoint col7. Perpendicular vertical? Output extends horizontal to left, not perpendicular! Wait no, output extends existing horizontal line along its own direction, not perpendicular. Hmm maybe for horizontal line, extend along its length at midpoint? Let's re-evaluate Ex3: Existing horizontal 2 at row7 cols3-11. Output row7 cols0-11 filled with 2: extends horizontally left. This is along the line's direction, not perpendicular. If applying "extend line from midpoint toward nearest edge perpendicular" would make vertical line at col? Not output.

Maybe I mis-selected: In Ex3, longest segment is horizontal 2. Its midpoint column is 7. Output extends along horizontal direction at row7 to left edge. Why left? Because there is an object above at col8? Hmm.

Let's consider alternative: Extend the longest line segment to the border in direction where it is closer? Ex3 horizontal 2 spans cols3-11. It is closer to left edge (distance 3) than right edge (4 cells to col15? right gap cols12-15 =4). Output extends left to edge. Yes! It extends horizontal segment to nearer edge. Example2 vertical 8 spans rows3-9 (length7). Closer to top edge distance3 (rows0-2) vs bottom edge distance4 (rows10-13). But output extends horizontally left at midpoint row6, not vertically to nearer top/bottom. So no.

Wait in Ex2 output added horizontal at row6, not extending vertical 8 along its axis. Why? Maybe because there is a horizontal segment color1 at bottom left length4. It might be longest? Compare lengths:
Ex2: color8 vertical length7 (rows3-9). color7 vertical length5 (rows0-4). color1 horizontal length4. Longest is 8. Output extends 8 horizontally at its midpoint left. This is perpendicular. Ex1 longest 4 vertical length9, output perpendicular horizontal. Ex3 nonzero lengths: color2 horizontal length9 (cols3-11). color5 vertical length3. Other singletons. Longest is 2 horizontal. If rule perpendicular, output should vertical line at midpoint col7, not horizontal. But output extends horizontally. Wait check Ex3 input row7: [0,0,0,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,0,0,0,0], indices 3..11 =2 length9. Output row7: [2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,0,0,0,0] indices 0..11 =2. That's same horizontal line extended left. So for horizontal longest, extension along axis. For vertical longest in Ex1/2, extension perpendicular? Contradiction.

Maybe I misread output Ex1: longest 4 vertical; output horizontal at row5. Could it be extending the *other* line (color2 vertical) perpendicular? Color2 at col0 rows4-6 length3. Its midpoint row5. Output horizontal row5 from col1 to col10 color4, not color2. Hmm it connects midpoint of color2 to longest vertical? The added line color is 4 (longest), direction from longest to shorter? 

Ex2 longest 8 vertical; output horizontal row6 from left edge to col4 color8. It is perpendicular to longest, at its midpoint. Why not along vertical? Could be because longest vertical is already near top/bottom? Let's inspect if any other object indicates direction: color1 horizontal at row12 cols0-3. Its midpoint col1. Maybe align? Output row6? no.

Maybe the task: Draw a line from the *center* of one object to the *center* of another object using color of larger object? Let's compute centers.
Ex1: color4 vertical center (5,10). color2 vertical center (5,0). Same row! Output connects centers with color4: row5 col1-10. Yes! It connects centers of two objects aligned horizontally. Color6 singleton and 7 maybe irrelevant noise.
Ex2: color8 vertical center (6,4). color1 horizontal center? row12 cols0-3 center (12,1.5). Not aligned with 8. color7 vertical center (2,7). color8 center (6,4). Not aligned. Output row6 col0-4 connects center of 8 to left edge, not another object. But maybe color1 horizontal indicates row? no.

Maybe centers of objects of same dimension? Ex1 two vertical lines aligned? color4 center row5, color2 center row5. Output connects them. Ex2 vertical 8 center row6. Is there another object whose column equals? color1 horizontal at row12, center col? no. color7 vertical center row2. Maybe no aligned object, extends to edge.

Ex3: color2 horizontal center col7 (row7, cols3-11 => center col7). Any object center at col7? color6 singleton at (4,8), not. color5 vertical center (1,1). color8 pair center (0.5,14.5). Output extends horizontal 2 from col0 to col11, i.e. connects center? It extends left to edge because maybe nearest edge. Hmm.

Maybe principle: Find longest straight line segment, extend it perpendicular? But Ex3 longest horizontal would output vertical, not. Let's check if color2 horizontal in Ex3 maybe actually two segments? Row7 cols3-11. Output extends left to col0, making length12. Could be not "extension" but moving/rotating? Hmm.

Let's list all examples as ARC maybe rule is "extend the largest object in direction of nearest border, to make it touch border." Ex1 largest vertical 4 at col10 touches right border already. Its nearest border along perpendicular? At row5, nearest border left? Distance to left 10, right 0 (touches right). But output extends horizontal left to border? It stops at col1 due to color2, not border col0. If no obstacle, would extend to left border. So it extends largest object perpendicular toward nearest border that is not already touched? Ex1 vertical touches right border; perpendicular row has nearest left border? It extends left until obstacle.
Ex2 largest vertical 8 at col4. It does not touch any border? Top/bottom: rows3-9, distance to top3, bottom4. Along its own axis nearest top. But output extends perpendicular left (distance4 to left edge) not top. Why? Maybe because vertical 8 already starts row3, closer to top but there is color7 above? Actually row0-4 col7, not in same column. It could extend up to row? But output left. Maybe because there is no obstacle left, extends to left border. Why not up? Maybe choose direction based on orientation of a "pointer" object? There is horizontal color1 at row12 below, indicating horizontal extension? Hmm.

Maybe examples show transformations involving "line segment that has a gap to border; fill row/column of its midpoint until border/obstacle." Which line chosen? Maybe the one with odd length? Ex1 4 length9 odd, 2 length3 odd. Ex2 8 length7 odd, 7 length5 odd, 1 length4 even. Ex3 2 length9 odd, 5 length3 odd. Longest odd. Output extends along a line through its midpoint perpendicular to its orientation? Wait Ex3 longest 2 is horizontal, midpoint column7. Perpendicular would be vertical at col7. But output extends horizontal. Why? Maybe because longest is horizontal, extension is along its orientation; if vertical, extension is perpendicular? That seems inconsistent.

Let's re-examine Ex3 output: row7 cols0-11 filled 2. Is that maybe a vertical line from midpoint of color5 to color2? Color5 vertical at col1 rows0-2. Its midpoint row1. Not row7. Color6 at (4,8). No.

Maybe there is a hidden same shape: The output completes a rectangle or line connecting objects based on "center of mass" of all nonzero? Let's compute bounding box and fill row/col through center?
Ex1 all nonzero bbox rows0-10 cols0-10. Center row5 col5. Output row5 (center row) filled with color4 from col1 to10. Color4 is rightmost object. Row5 is center row of grid/bbox. It fills from col1 to right edge? Actually bbox center row=5. So output fills center row with color of object at right edge? Ex1 yes.
Ex2 all nonzero bbox rows0-12 cols0-9? Nonzero color1 at row12, col7 at col7, color8 col4. bbox rows0-12 cols0-7? center row6, center col3? Output row6 filled 8 cols0-4. Row6 is center row of bbox (0+12)/2=6. Color8 is at col4. Fills row6 from left edge to col4. Hmm.
Ex3 bbox rows0-7 cols0-15? center row3.5, center col7.5. Output row7 (bottom of bbox), not center. It extends horizontal 2 at row7. Maybe bbox center col? 7.5, row7 is object row.

Maybe not.

Let's search memory: ARC tasks with extending lines from "pointers". Often: There are line segments and single pixels. For each single pixel, project a line from it to a segment? Or use single pixel as indicator to extend line segment to border.

Example1: singleton 6 at (0,5). Its column 5. There is vertical 4 at col10. Could draw horizontal from 4 at row5 to left until hit color2. The singleton's column gives row? Yes row5. Color? output uses color of vertical line (4), not singleton. Singleton 7 at (10,3) maybe row10? column3? Not used? Maybe there are two markers: one color6 at top, one color7 bottom. They define row? Hmm 6 at col5 -> row5; 7 at row10 col3 maybe? no.

Example2: singleton? There is horizontal color1 segment row12 cols0-3; maybe acts as marker indicating row? Output row6. Could row6 = (row12 -?)/2? Color7 vertical top at col7 length5; color8 vertical at col4 length7. Output horizontal row6, left to edge. Row6 maybe bottom of color7? no.

Example3: singleton color6 at (4,8). Output row7, not.

Let's isolate objects:
Example1:
- A: color6 single at (0,5)
- B: color4 vertical col10 rows1-9
- C: color2 vertical col0 rows4-6
- D: color7 single at (10,3)

Output modifies B? Actually adds horizontal row5 with color4 from col1-10. This horizontal line is at row5, which is the row index of center of C and B. It connects B to C. It also passes under color6? color6 col5 not on row5. D no.

Example2:
- A: color7 vertical col7 rows0-4
- B: color8 vertical col4 rows3-9
- C: color1 horizontal row12 cols0-3
Output adds horizontal row6 with color8 from col0-4. Row6 is center of B. It connects B to left edge. Why no connection to A/C? A at col7 right, center row2; C bottom.

Example3:
- A: color5 vertical col1 rows0-2
- B: color8 cells (0,15),(1,14) diagonal
- C: color6 single (4,8)
- D: color2 horizontal row7 cols3-11
Output extends D left to edge. Row7 is its own row. It connects D to left edge? There is color5 at col1 rows0-2, not same row. No obstacle. So extension along its axis to left edge.

Maybe rule: For the longest line segment in grid, if it's vertical, extend a horizontal line at its midpoint until border/obstacle; if horizontal, extend vertically at its midpoint? Ex3 would vertical at col7. Not.

Wait output Ex3 extends D left, but D's midpoint col7. Maybe vertical at col7 would intersect color6 at (4,8)? Not exact. If using center of C? C at (4,8), D spans cols3-11. C is above row7 col8, not col7. Output could be extending D left because C is at col8 indicating direction? no.

Maybe longest D horizontal is at row7. It extends left because there is another horizontal object C? Actually C is single at row4 col8, near right of D. It might indicate extend right? But output left.

Let's consider maybe output completes a rectangle border? Example1 output row5 from col1-10 creates a horizontal line between vertical 2 and 4. It forms rectangle-ish? Input has left vertical 2 rows4-6 and right vertical 4 rows1-9. Output makes row5 bridge, creating "H" shape? Yes: vertical 2 (left) and vertical 4 (right) connected at middle row -> H. Example2: input has vertical 8 at col4 rows3-9; output adds horizontal left at row6 to edge. Not H. But there is horizontal 1 at bottom left row12. Maybe if connected to left edge, forms L? Example3: horizontal 2 row7 extended left to edge, maybe with vertical 5 at col1 top forms? Not.

Could connect at midpoint row6? But vertical 7 doesn't extend to row6. Maybe extend to nearest parallel? It would go right to col7? Output goes left. So no.

Ex3 longest horizontal 2 has no parallel horizontal? There is color5 vertical, diagonal, singleton. So extends to nearest border left.

Maybe rule: Extend the longest line segment to the nearest border/obstacle along the *same orientation*? Ex1 longest vertical 4: same orientation vertical. It is at col10, already touches? Actually vertical segment rows1-9, not entire column; nearest border top row0 distance1, bottom row10 distance1? Output horizontal not. Ex2 vertical 8 rows3-9; nearest border top distance3, bottom distance4. Output horizontal. So no.

Maybe there is a pattern of colors: 6,4,2,7 in ex1; 7,8,1 ex2; 5,8,6,2 ex3. Maybe colors indicate directions? In ARC, colors arbitrary. But maybe single pixels with colors 6 and 7 are markers? Example1 has 6 at top and 7 at bottom; output uses row5 = col of 6. Example2 no 6/7 single except 7 vertical. Ex3 has 6 singleton and 8 diagonal.

Ex2 added row = 6. Sources: midpoint of vertical 8=6; grid center row=(0+13)/2=6.5 -> row6 or7; bbox center row=(0+12)/2=6.

General: For longest segment, draw a line through its center, perpendicular to the segment? No, for horizontal, perpendicular would column. Instead maybe draw a line through its center in the direction of the shorter dimension? Hmm.

Maybe "extend the longest straight object in both directions until border/obstacle, but if it's vertical, rotate 90 and extend horizontally"? That seems weird.

Maybe the transformation is: Find the longest *line of nonzero contiguous in a row or column*. Extend it in the direction where there is another line of same color? Ex2 longest vertical 8 spans rows3-9. Nearest edge along its orientation is top (3 cells) vs bottom (4 cells). But output extends horizontally left, not vertical top. So not.

Let's look at objects as letters/numbers? Colors maybe not arbitrary? Example1 colors 2,4,6,7. Ex2 1,7,8. Ex3 2,5,6,8. Maybe colors encode orientation? In ARC, colors could be any. Output adds horizontal at midpoint to left until edge. Ex3 selected 2 horizontal. Output adds horizontal? Wait if rule is extend selected object perpendicular? Ex3 would vertical at midpoint. But output extends selected object itself left. Hmm maybe because selected object is horizontal, and extension direction is along orientation; for vertical, extension is perpendicular? No.

In Ex1 selected vertical 4 is not extended along length; instead a new horizontal of same color at midpoint. Why? Maybe because vertical 4 is already at right edge; extending along length would go up/down to nearest edge? It could extend up to row0 or down to row10. But output horizontal. Wait vertical 4 spans rows1-9. It is missing row0 and row10 in col10. Nearest top gap 1 (row0 col10) and bottom gap1 (row10 col10). It could extend to both? Output doesn't. So not.

Maybe transformation is not about selected object orientation; rather it draws a line from the selected object to the *nearest border* in the direction of the center of the grid? Let's test:
Ex1 selected 4 at (center row5,col10). Grid center (5,5). From selected center, direction to grid center is left. Output draws left from selected to obstacle. Yes.
Ex2 selected 8 at (6,4). Grid center (6.5,4.5) or bbox center (6,3.5). Direction to grid center is maybe right/down. Output draws left. Not.

Nearest bottom. Output draws left, not nearest. Hmm.

Opposite? Example2: pointer? color1 horizontal at (12,1.5) below-left of selected 8 (6,4). Output extends left (toward pointer's left side). Example1: pointer? color6 at (0,5) above selected 4 (5,10); output left. Not.

- Identify the longest contiguous line segment of a single color (possibly even color).
- Extend it by drawing a line of same color from its center perpendicular? Wait Ex3 contradicts. Could the longest in Ex3 be vertical? Count contiguous 2s: row7 has nine 2s. Maybe there is also a vertical line of 2s? No, only row7. So no.
- Maybe the rule is to "rotate" the longest segment 90 degrees around its center? Ex1 vertical 4 length9 -> horizontal 4 length? Output horizontal from col1 to10 length10, centered at col5.5? Draw a line through center to the nearest border, but choose orientation that is perpendicular if the segment is vertical, parallel if horizontal? Why asymmetry? Maybe because all selected verticals in examples are at columns nearer right/left; selected horizontal in Ex3 is at row7 near bottom? Hmm.

Maybe because there is an odd-colored object on the right? Ex1 odd 6 at col5? not. Ex2 odd 7 at col7 (right of 8). Ex3 odd 5 at col1 (left) and 6 at col8. Hmm.

Ex2 adds row6 col0-4: to left of vertical 8 at col4 to edge.
Ex3 adds row7 col0-2: to left of horizontal 2 at col3? Wait output row7 col0-11 fills also existing cols3-11; the new part is col0-2 to left of existing horizontal segment start col3. The target is the longest even-colored object? In Ex1 target vertical 4, but extension is perpendicular left from its center. In Ex2 target vertical 8, perpendicular left from center. In Ex3 target horizontal 2, parallel left from its row. Hmm.

Why Ex1 not parallel left from vertical 4? Vertical 4 cannot extend left as it's vertical; "extend leftward" might mean draw horizontal from its middle to left. If object vertical, line is horizontal through its midpoint; if object horizontal, line is along its row. But for horizontal, its row is not center? It is its row. So general: from the target object, extend leftwards in the grid at the row of its center. For vertical object center has row; draw horizontal left. For horizontal object center row is its row; draw horizontal left (over existing, extending). That fits all! Target = largest object (maybe longest segment). Then draw horizontal line to the left from the rightmost extent? Let's formalize:
- Choose the longest straight colored segment.
- Determine its center row (for vertical) or row (for horizontal). Actually any object has a center row.
